questions.stem: A nurse is planning discharge for a client with unstable housing and no reliable transportation to follow-up visits. Which concept best explains why these issues should be incorporated into the care plan?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Health literacy, because the central issue is whether the client can understand written instructions and medication labels after discharge.","B":"Social determinants of health, because housing and transportation access can directly affect follow-up care and health outcomes after discharge.","C":"Utilization review, because the primary issue is whether the hospitalization met payer criteria rather than barriers the client will face at home.","D":"Informed consent, because the central issue is the client's legal authorization for treatment rather than access to housing or transportation."}}
questions.rationale: Healthy People 2030 defines social determinants of health as conditions in the environments where people live and identifies housing and transportation as examples that affect health and well-being. These barriers therefore belong in discharge planning. Health literacy concerns finding, understanding, and using health information; utilization review concerns use of health services; and informed consent concerns authorization for care rather than access barriers after discharge.
questions.source_name: HHS ODPHP — Healthy People 2030: Social Determinants of Health
questions.source_detail: Healthy People 2030 identifies safe housing and transportation as social determinants of health and states that SDOH substantially affect health, well-being, and quality of life.

questions.stem: A previously normotensive pregnant client at 32 weeks has a blood pressure of 148/94 mm Hg on two occasions 4 hours apart, new proteinuria, a severe headache that persists despite medication, and visual spots. Which diagnosis is most consistent with these findings?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Preeclampsia with severe features, because new hypertension after 20 weeks plus proteinuria and persistent neurologic symptoms supports this diagnosis.","B":"Gestational hypertension without severe features, because proteinuria and persistent neurologic symptoms do not change the diagnosis once hypertension begins.","C":"Chronic hypertension, because blood pressure first detected after 20 weeks with new proteinuria is presumed to have been present before pregnancy.","D":"Gestational diabetes, because hypertension, proteinuria, headache, and visual symptoms are a typical cluster of findings caused by maternal hyperglycemia."}}
questions.rationale: ACOG defines preeclampsia using new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or specified end-organ findings. Severe features include a new-onset headache unresponsive to medication and not explained by another diagnosis, or visual symptoms. Gestational hypertension lacks proteinuria or severe end-organ findings, chronic hypertension predates pregnancy or is identified before 20 weeks, and gestational diabetes does not explain this hypertensive neurologic presentation.
questions.source_name: ACOG — Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia
questions.source_detail: ACOG criteria include blood pressure at least 140/90 mm Hg on two occasions at least 4 hours apart after 20 weeks plus proteinuria or end-organ findings; severe features include persistent treatment-resistant headache or visual symptoms.

questions.stem: A pregnant client at 34 weeks with intact membranes has sudden, painless, bright-red vaginal bleeding. The uterus is nontender and the fetal heart tracing is reassuring. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Placental abruption, because third-trimester bleeding is most often painless when the placenta separates from the uterine wall.","B":"Vasa previa, because painless bleeding with intact membranes and a reassuring fetal heart rate is the usual presentation before vessel rupture.","C":"Bloody show from labor, because a sudden moderate amount of bright-red blood without contractions or cervical change is expected near term.","D":"Placenta previa, because sudden painless bright-red vaginal bleeding in the second half of pregnancy is a characteristic presentation."}}
questions.rationale: Placenta previa classically causes sudden, painless vaginal bleeding in the second or third trimester and should be evaluated with ultrasonography before any digital cervical examination. Placental abruption more often causes pain or uterine tenderness. Vasa previa classically becomes apparent with bleeding around membrane rupture and fetal instability, while bloody show is typically blood-tinged mucus associated with cervical change rather than unexplained bright-red bleeding.
questions.source_name: Merck Manual Professional Edition — Placenta Previa
questions.source_detail: Merck states that placenta previa typically manifests as sudden painless vaginal bleeding after 20 weeks and recommends ultrasonography for diagnosis before digital cervical examination.

questions.stem: A multiparous client gives birth 2 hours 45 minutes after regular contractions began, with rapid cervical dilation and fetal descent. Which labor pattern best describes this course?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Precipitous labor, because labor and delivery occurring in less than 3 hours from the onset of regular contractions fits this definition.","B":"Protracted active-phase labor, because very rapid cervical dilation over a short interval meets the criteria for abnormally slow progress.","C":"Active-phase arrest, because complete dilation after rapidly progressive contractions indicates that cervical change has stopped.","D":"Uterine tachysystole, because a short total labor duration by itself establishes more than five contractions in 10 minutes."}}
questions.rationale: NCBI Bookshelf defines precipitous labor as extremely rapid labor and delivery, usually less than 3 hours from the start of regular contractions to birth. Protracted labor and active-phase arrest describe abnormally slow or absent cervical progress. Uterine tachysystole is defined by excessive contraction frequency, not by the total duration of labor.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Health Promotion: Labor & Delivery Care
questions.source_detail: The NCBI Bookshelf labor-and-delivery chapter defines precipitous labor as labor and delivery that are extremely rapid, usually less than 3 hours from the start of contractions to birth.

questions.stem: A newborn is assigned Apgar scores at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth. Which set lists the five components used in the Apgar score?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Heart rate, respiratory effort, blood pressure, temperature, and birth weight, which together quantify the newborn's immediate transition.","B":"Heart rate, respiratory effort, gestational age, birth weight, and head circumference, which together form the standard Apgar assessment.","C":"Heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, temperature, and muscle tone, which together are scored at 1 and 5 minutes after birth.","D":"Heart rate, respiratory effort, muscle tone, reflex irritability, and color, which are the five standard components of the Apgar score."}}
questions.rationale: ACOG and the American Academy of Pediatrics define the Apgar score using five components: color, heart rate, reflexes or reflex irritability, muscle tone, and respiration or respiratory effort. The score is reported at 1 and 5 minutes after birth. Blood pressure, temperature, birth weight, gestational age, oxygen saturation, glucose, and head circumference are not Apgar components.
questions.source_detail: The joint ACOG/AAP statement lists color, heart rate, reflexes, muscle tone, and respiration as the five Apgar components and states that scores are reported at 1 and 5 minutes after birth.
